I am interested in the federal penitentiary case file record of Marcel Aveline. Finding aid information: TITLE/DESCRIPTION: Marcel Aveline. REFERENCE NUMBER: RG73 1985-86/162 1. Aveline was born between 1910 and 1914 in Québec, and was repeatedly incarcerated at federal prisons in Québec and Ontario between the late 1920s until c. 1970. Aveline was a well-known figure in the 1930s and 40s, leading highly public protests at federal prisons. As a frequent prisoner, Aveline was only the second Québecois (and one of the first nation-wide) to be designated a 'habitual offender' and given a life sentence. His time in prison coincides with enormous changes in the Canadian penal system, so I hope his case file will be revealing of these broader trends.

RE: Access to Information Act Request, Report of the Superintendent Penitentiaries, 1932  I write to make an Access to Information Act request regarding the following documents held by Library and Archives Canada:   TITLE/DESCRIPTION: REPORT OF THE SUPERINTENDENT OF ; PENITENTIARIES ON THE KINGSTON ; PENITENTIARY DISTURBANCES 1932 REPORTS BY DM ORMOND, SUPERINTENDENT OF PENITENTIARIES OF DEC. 6, 1932 (72 PAGES) & JAN. 23, 1933 (39 PAGES) TO THE MINISTER OF JUSTICE ON THE HISTORY OF DISTURBANCES AT THE KINGSTON PENITENTIARY AND RESULTS OF AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE RIOT OF OCT. 13, 1932. COPY OF THE PUBLISHED REPORT OF ORMOND IN 1933. TRANSCRIPT (16 PAGES) OF AN INTERVIEW HELD BY MEMBERS OF THE CANADA LABOUR DEFENCE LEAGUE WITH THE MINISTER OF JUSTICE ON OCT. 26, 1932 AT HIS OFFICE.   Reference Number: RG13 2000-01038-5  Access Code: 32 - Restricted by Law  I am requesting that this document be reviewed and released.  Beyond the usual considerations, I wish to provide you with some information showing that these documents were public at the time they were created and should not be so treated as private now.  The first two documents, reports by the Superintendent of Penitentiaries to the Minister of Justice, were available to the public and discussed in the media. For example, see statements made by Minister of Justice Hugh Guthrie in open Parliament on 6 February 1933 where he ordered 750 copies of the report to be produced for distribution, and discussion of these reports in open Parliament in the weeks that followed. Reporters who had reviewed the document in full also discussed the content of the report in the newspapers of the day. See, for example, "Slur on Private Soldier Seen in Prison Report," The Globe, 16 February 1933. The title/description of the document also notes that Ormond's report was published.  The transcript of the Canadian Labour Defence League visit to Guthrie also should not be restricted. Guthrie had a government stenographer attend the meeting and invited reporters into the room during the meeting. See, for example, "Communists Well but Won't Allow them to be Seen," Toronto Daily Star, 26 October 1932, and E. Cecil-Smith, "Guthrie on Kingston Penitentiary," The Canadian Labor Defender (November 1932).

We would therefore be grateful if you would send us any relevant documents contained in accession 2002-00101-4 deposited at the National Archives of Canada. We also know that the Department of Health Canada carried out inspections there to assess general sanitary conditions, notably on May 1, 1985, as part of its Indian health services monitoring program. Medical Services for the Quebec Region also had bacteriological analyzes of water samples taken at the residence, including on May 27, 1985. We would be grateful if you would send us all the documents in your possession concerning the residence of Louvicourt, including any document concerning the planning of its operation or concerning its closure.

His wife, Hideno Takenaka has an index card on reel c9303, index card #2879. Her case file is #3810, which is on reel c9338. It is also not digitized. Both have been dead for a long time.

All documents in English and French in Elections Canada’s possession or control, including all correspondence, all notes (handwritten or otherwise), all emails and electronic correspondence, all memoranda, and all other matter of documents or communications, including in electronic format, that concern  recommendation A23 of the 2016 Elections Canada report entitled, An Electoral Framework for the 21st Century–Recommendations from the Chief Electoral Officer of Canada Following the 42nd General Election, which is available online. Under recommendation A23, the report recommends modifications to the residency requirements for returning officers. Currently, under section 22 of the Canada Elections Act, returning officers (RO), assistant returning officers (ARO) and additional assistant returning officers (AARO), are required to reside in the electoral district in which he or she is to perform duties under this Act.  Recommendation A23 is that the residency requirement for ROs, AROs and AAROs should be replaced with a requirement that they reside in the electoral district where appointed or in an adjacent electoral district.

documentcloud_description:
Imagine this fictitious example: a Government of Canada employee is blind  enrolled in a Canada School of Public Class. The online class material has  pictures of northern coast lines which the course developer is using to teach something important about the relationship between climate change and policy. The student is an accomplished geoscientist and the CSPS needs to give her equivalent alternative text so she can learn.  This example illustrates the requirement of the CSPS to provide equivalent alternative text. 
Provide:
a) Five recent examples of the Canada School of Public Service provide equivalent, alternative text for learners with sight loss. These should include i) the non-text entity (e.g., graph, image) and the ii) the equivalent alternative text.  At least two of these should be for complex images (rather than charts or diagrams)
b) If an external alternative text provider was hired to create the text, please provide sufficient documents (e.g., invoice) to know the company's name/location.
c) All CSPS policies and guidelines and training materials for providing equivalent, alternative text for learners with sight loss. 

Per 4.(2.1), please ensure any PDFs are OCR'ed so they are usable by people with disabilities who rely on screen readers. If you don't know what a screen reader is, please read here: https://axesslab.com/what-is-a-screen-reader/
Likewise,ensure the non-text entity (e.g., graph, image, etc.) is in vibrant color.

documentcloud_title: 2022-05 – AF-2021-00177 – Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation
documentcloud_description:
All documentation, included but not limited to correspondence, emails, recommendations, responses, conferences, symposia, memos, policy documents, action plans, briefing notes, images, plans, reports or studies related to and/or mentioning: 
Urban, regional and/or community planning and subdivision and design review activities of CMHC and its employees from 1946 to approximately 1970 both individually and/or jointly with Wartime Housing Limited and/or the Community Planning Association of Canada. 

This request is part of a SSHRC-funded academic research project from a Queen's University professor titled "How Canada Became a Suburban Nation: The Role of the Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation in Reviewing Canadian Community Planning" It is widely acknowledged that Canada is now a "suburban nation", but how did it make the transition from urban to suburban so quickly after World War II? The Central Mortgage and Housing Corporation was established as a federal Crown agency to implement national housing objectives in the post-war recovery period. However, CMHC was also tasked with implementing the federal government's national community planning objectives. The agency played a major role in transforming Canada into a suburban nation by 1980. CMHC reinforced the suburban trajectory by publishing planning handbooks, establishing national standards, seeding a national network of planning schools, importing planners and designing and developing federal lands.

4. All final versions of the records referred to in bullets 1-3, developed by joint review panels.

REQUEST. Provide access to any and all Station Blackout Reports (SBOs) in 2003 and emerging IRS Reports generated by the CNSC pertaining to the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station “A” (units I to 4) and the Pickering Nuclear Generating Station “B” (units 5 to 8).

2003 STATION BLACKOUT (SBO) AT NUCLEAR POWER PLANT.

BACKGROUND. A station blackout is defined as a plant condition with
complete loss of all AC power from the preferred offsite AC sources, from the main generator and from standby AC power sources important to safety to the essential and nonessential switchgear buses. DC power supplies and uninterruptible AC 34 power supplies may be available as long as batteries can supply the loads. Alternate AC power supplies are available. SBOs have traditionally been underreported but according to the IAEA, these are occurring at frequencies above that what traditionally would be considered as normal. There are several safety aspects associated with SBO events which may lead to the deterioration of key safety functions. An SBO event can lead to a severe accident if there are complications in the restoration of electrical power to plant buses within the coping time. The loss of grid is generally an initiating event and coincidental failure of onsite AC power supplies results in an SBO.

documentcloud_title: 2023-06 – A-2022-26493 – Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
documentcloud_description: In 2020, Canada significantly limited opportunities for air travel to Canada as well as immigration services in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2021, the IRCC’s Ministerial Centre for MPs and Senators (MCMPS) temporarily interrupted its services in response to the humanitarian and migrant crisis in Afghanistan in order to reassign staff to these efforts. In 2022, the MCMPS again reassigned staff to special units to respond to the humanitarian and migrant crisis in Ukraine. We are requesting any documents from 2019 to date showing, for each of these three crises, the following information regarding the MCMPS: *The number of employees assigned to MCMPS services before, during and after the crises; *The call volumes received annually or monthly at the MCMPS before, during and after the crises;*The volume of emails received annually or monthly at the MCMPS before, during and after the crises. Following these crises, a number of reassignments and limits to accessing the MCMPS were implemented in order to manage  case volumes. Without a doubt, the managers making these decisions had all the data available to them that we have discussed here in order to make the necessary administrative decisions. As a result, these documents containing this data have undoubtedly been discussed and shared.

documentcloud_title: 2023-08 – A-2022-00052 – Transportation Safety Board of Canada
documentcloud_description: I am seeking information regarding the following aircraft incident: at 1:46 p.m. on 15 November 2021, a privately registered Cessna R182 aircraft (registration C-FBKJ, serial number R18200149) departed on a visual flight rules (VFR) flight plan from Nanaimo Airport (CYCD), British Columbia (BC), to Glacier Park International Airport (KGPI), Montana, United States. The filed flight plan showed a direct route from CYCD to KGPI, flown at an altitude of 10 500 feet above sea level (ASL). A pilot and 1 passenger were on board. The aircraft crashed. A TSB investigation was conducted regarding the incident (Air transportation safety investigation report A21P0124). I am specifically looking for the following: a copy of the flight plan, a copy of the TSB Laboratory Report LP171/2021 including an electronic copy of all data used in the production of LP171/2021, Digital copies of all on-scene photographs taken by the TSB investigators, (copies of digital images, a copy of investigators notes, a copy of any radar data obtained for the investigation, a transcript of any conversations between the pilot and air traffic control, a copy of the aircraft Journey Logbook, a copy of the aircraft Technical Logbooks, a copy of any insurance certificate/proof of insurance, correspondence between Nav Canada and the TSB, correspondence between any insurance adjuster and/or Underwriter and the TSB

documentcloud_title: 2023-07 – A-2022-05111 – Patented Medicine Prices Review Board Canada
documentcloud_description:
Electronic copies of the following documents. In all cases,  cabinet confidences may be excluded and draft versions of documents. In all of the requests below, “draft guidelines” refers to the PMPRB Guidelines that were published for comment on October 6, 2022, or any prior drafts or versions of those 2022 Guidelines (for example, if a draft version was circulated to Health Canada for comment in September 2022, it would be part of the “draft guidelines” for the purpose of this request).
 • Emails or other communications from Health Canada commenting on the draft guidelines, and that were sent between July 1, 2022, and October 6, 2022. 
 • Emails or other communications from the Board members or Board Chair commenting on the draft guidelines, and that were sent between July 1, 2022, and October 6, 2022. 
 • Any training presentations, training manuals, or summaries of the new guidelines prepared for use by the Board Staff, Board, or other governmental departments prepared between July 1, 2022, and October 6, 2022.
 • Any documents with calculations of how much prices will decrease under the draft guidelines, or under alternative pricing rules, and that were prepared between January 1, 2022, and October 6, 2022 (note the change in date relative to other requests). 
• Any documents comparing prices or price reductions under the draft guidelines and the old PMPRB Compendium of Guidelines and Procedures. 
• Any documents, including legal memos, on the compliance of the draft guidelines with legal decisions about the PMPRB, including Alexion Pharmaceuticals Inc. v. Canada (Attorney General), 2021 FCA 157, Merck Canada c Canada, 2022 QCCA 240, and Innovative Medicines Canada v. Canada (Attorney General), 2020 FC 725. 
• Any documents which discuss how a medicine’s therapeutic class and comparator products will be established under the draft guidelines. 
• Any documents showing how the Board Staff arrived at the exact pricing tests discussed in paragraph 33-35 of the draft Guidelines. 
• Any documents which discuss how Board Staff will assess whether a price is excessive *after* an investigation has been opened. For context, the backgrounder which accompanied the draft guidelines suggested that staff will consider “the totality of the circumstances surrounding the price of the medicine, through the lens of the section 85 factors.
documentcloud_source: Patented Medicine Prices Review Board Canada

Please provide all CNSC internal correspondence and also CNSC correspondence with AECL, CNL, IAEA, Vienna Permanent Mission and any Canadian or foreign government department or private company (emails, reports, phone transcripts, presentations) containing information since January 2016, regarding: 1. The International Independent Peer Review (IIPR) of the NSDF at Chalk River; and 2. The proposed IAEA ARTEMIS review mission for the NSDF at Chalk River. The following specific information is requested:  A) The proposed scope of the ARTEMIS review of CNL’s NSDF safety case, envisaged by the last bullet of slide 27 of the CNSC presentation of May 17, 2018: Canadian Update to the International Nuclear Regulators Association, Gyeongju, Republic of Korea, e-Doc 5514465. B) Prior correspondence, relating to page 9 of the August 13, 2019, e-mail of ATIP-2019-00054AI reference to the 2017 CNSC initiative for an independent third party review of the NSDF by the IAEA. C) All correspondence prior to and subsequent to p. 11 of the email of November 2, 2017, ATIP-2019-00054AI, relating to the CNSC payment of and discussions with the IAEA for the ARTEMIS NSDF peer review, including information on the changes made leading to the withdrawal of the ARTEMIS review proposal. Information already provided in ATIP-2019-00054AI is not required. The CNSC presentation of May 17, 2018, e-Doc 5514465 is also not required.

During an exercise (I believe it was RIMPAC 96) all Canadian & International participant ships were forced to take shelter / return to port early due to a severe storm. The CO of HMCS Cowichan opted to return to CFB Esquimalt. During the return voyage from the central west coast of Vancouver Island to Victoria, HMCS Cowichan sustained significant damage to the ship, several crew members were injured and MARS training officers were aboard forced to remain in their mess deck. I would like to receive any information, damage repairs, injuries to sailor, circumstance/decision making reports that were generated regarding this event. Between 01- 03-1996 and 31-10-1996

All and any information on the following accident. WINNIPEG, Manitoba, June 25 (Canadian Press)—Nine persons, seven of them Indian high school students, were killed yesterday when a twin-engine plane crashed and burned on a residential street shortly after taking off from Winnipeg airport. The dead included the pilot of the Beechcraft 18, owned by Ilford-Riveiton Airways. The other victim was a nurse. The plane crashed into a tree between two houses in west Winnipeg, not far from the end of the runway. Both houses were damaged in the ensuing fire, but no one on the ground was injured. The plane had taken off on a flight to Oxford House in northeastern Manitoba, Witnesses said its engines were sputtering and it appeared to be in a banking turn just before the crash. It was returning the Indian students to their homes in the North after a year of high school studies in southern Manitoba. The Library and Archives Canada has these records and I am requesting this information from them. (RG12) images 648 and 649 of this page: 135953_Boite-Box21_1972.pdf (archives.ca). The complete reference is 1996-04098-7 box 3 file 5002-H-20001.

documentcloud_title: 2024-05 – AF-2023-00120 – Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation
documentcloud_description:
I am reaching out to seek your assistance in obtaining information from CMHC regarding the federal government's Limited Dividend Program. This program played a crucial role in delivering low to moderate rental units to the market, starting in the late 1930s, and was a significant part of the Assisted Private Rental Program, initiated with the National Housing Act in 1938 under Section 15 (formerly Section 13, Limited Dividend). Originally financed through a combination of federal and private loans, the program underwent a transformative shift in 1954 when it became exclusively supported by a direct federal loan. In my pursuit of a thorough understanding of this historical initiative, I am seeking any available data that the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation (CMHC) might possess. 
Specifically, I am interested in the following details: 
1. Names(corporations) of the recipients of the Limited Dividend Program. 
2. Addresses of the properties where the low to moderate rental units were built. 
3. The number of rental units the program produced over its lifespan. 
4. Data on approved rental increases at each property over the life span of the program.

Henry Auger was a treaty member of one of the three bands that are now known collectively as Kapawe'no First Nation. The band came to fruition under chief Kinoosayo at Sucker Creek, AB. Many families split off to Swan Hills, Sucker Creek, Grouard and Driftpile. I am writing to seek the historical band lists (may also be called payee lists, or annuity lists) for the three reserves in Grouard - Pakashan, Halcro and Freeman; I am seeking all member names. Secondly, I would like to know what year Henry/Henry Auger signed onto the treaty, and what years he received treaty annuities. I would like to see all years to date starting from 1899 when Treaty 8 was signed at Grouard, AB. Henri/Henry Ambroise Auger was born on December 29, 1917, in Grouard, AB. He died on September 15, 1985, in Slave Lake, AB.

1) Telegrams sent from the Canadian consulate in Boston to the then Department of External Affairs on the reaction among New England fishermen, the New England Fishery Management Councils and New England politicians regarding East Coast Fisheries, fisheries management, the draft American-Canadian agreement on these issues and the boundary issue. The telegrams were sent by regular surface mail, but classified confidential. Copies likely exist both at External Affairs and in the Department of Fisheries and Oceans. Time frame: 1979-1980 – with a focus on March to December 1979.   (2) Department of External Affairs reports created in the Canadian Consulate General in Boston on three annual meetings of the Conference of Eastern Canadian Premiers and Northeastern Governors held in (1) Whitefield, New Hampshire (June 11-13, 1978); (2) Estérel, Quebec (June 26-27, 1979), and (3) Ferrisburg, Vermont (June 26-27, 1980). May be found within records of such cross-border political relations by lower levels of government, which occurred on the West Coast and possibly elsewhere. There is also a federal-provincial relations aspect. Time Frame: 1978-1980

documentcloud_description: Confirmation document, email, containing at least two Reports were sent to the Technical Specialist(s) covering Training Program(s), deemed qualified, and preparing the Gentillly II Nuclear Power Plant Integrated Safety Review (ISR) mandated by the IAEA; the two Reports are, as follows: Preliminary Event Report and the Detailed Event Report ; these two Reports covered the event that occurred on 27 October, 2009, at Gentilly II Nuclear Power Plant.

Clarified text on April 17, 2020:
Emails were to be sent to Specialist(s), as follows:

Safety Systems, Training Programs, Human Factors, and Quality Assurance.

The causes identified in the preliminary and detailed reports describes a minimum number of specialist(s) that should have been informed via email of the Event by providing to them the R-99.

We are reiterating our requests, as follows:

Emails that forwarded the R-99 to specialists,

Proof of receipt of emails to specialist, title of Experts, and 

Division to which they were attached to. In addition, kindly provide the ID Tag Number( specific identification, unique number) of the failed relay.

documentcloud_description:
This request seeks records pertaining to the CHRC’s policy, criteria, and operational procedures for the exercise of its discretionary power to reopen closed complaint files on its own initiative. 

The request is framed by a recent and material example of this power’s application: the Commission’s decision to reopen a series of files concerning the Temporary Public Policy for out-of-status construction workers in the Greater Toronto Area. This action underscores the necessity of public scrutiny into the lawful and consistent application of this significant power.

To elucidate the institutional framework governing this discretionary power, we respectfully request the following categories of records:
1. Policy and Operational Framework Records: All records that define, establish, or discuss the criteria, process, and legal authority for the CHRC to reopen a closed complaint file suo motu (on its own initiative). This includes, but is not limited to: operational directives; procedural manuals; policy statements; briefing notes; memoranda; reports that analyze the scope, limits, or application of this power; training materials, presentations, or guidance documents provided to staff or commissioners; records that can be referenced as “transparency and accountability” with specific rationale for reopening files.

2. Records Specific to the Recent Exercise of Power: All records that discuss, analyze, or authorize the specific decision to reopen files related to the Temporary Public Policy for out-of-status construction workers in the GTA. This includes, but is not limited to: internal correspondence; emails; memoranda; briefing notes; records documenting the deliberation, rationale, and approval process for this decision, including records sent to or from related to temporary public policy for out-of-status construction workers in the Greater Toronto Area; records containing legal advice, risk analysis, or policy considerations pertaining to this specific action.

Timeframe: from November 14, 2020, to November 14, 2025.

documentcloud_title: 2026-04 - A-2025-66437 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
documentcloud_description: I am requesting aggregate statistical records and any related briefing material concerning Express Entry invitation rounds and pool composition for the period 1 January 2024 to 18 September 2025, inclusive. A. Statistics requested For each Express Entry round of invitations (ITA round) between 2024-01-01 and 2025-09-18, provide the count of invitations to apply (ITAs) that were declined, allowed to expire, or otherwise not used by invitees. If IRCC tracks separate sub-categories (expired vs. actively declined vs. withdrawn after acceptance), please include each sub-total and a brief definition. As of 18 September 2025 (or the most recent extraction date available within five business days of that date), provide: Total number of active Express Entry profiles in the pool. Average CRS score of all active profiles. Number of active profiles with CRS > 500. (If readily available) a frequency table showing the number of profiles by CRS band (e.g., 0-300, 301-350, 501-550, 551-600, > 600). B. Related internal analyses Please provide any briefing notes, reports, risk assessments, or analytical slide decks prepared between 2023-01-01 and 2025-09-18 that discuss: The incidence of ITAs being declined, expired, or unused in Express Entry, and any operational or policy implications; and Potential misuse of the Express Entry system (e.g., creation of non-bona-fide or duplicate profiles) that could artificially inflate CRS score cut-offs. C. Preferred format Statistical tables in machine-readable form (Excel or CSV) where available. Briefing materials in PDF. D. Clarifications I am not requesting any personal information about individual candidates. Aggregate counts and anonymised tables are sufficient. If certain statistics are produced only for internal dashboards, please export the underlying tables (or screenshots if that is the only form available). E. Discretion to sever or clarify If portions of responsive records fall under a mandatory or discretionary exemption, please sever only the exempt portions and release the remainder.

documentcloud_description: Excluding transitory records inadvertently retained, please provide copies of all reports, notes and communications related to the following three items: 1) A meeting held on November 22, 2023 between the Vice Presidents of the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission (CNSC), the Impact Assessment Agency (IAAC or “the Agency”) and the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO) to discuss “areas of uncertainty NWMO has identified with respect to the regulatory process for the DGR project”. 2) A letter dated November 23, 2023 from President Swami to the Acting CEO of the CNSC and president of IAAC “regarding the activities that are needed to prepare for the regulatory process for NWMO’s DGR [Annex 1] and Table 1 and Table 2 found in Annex 1 of the letter dated November 23 3) A meeting held on November 29, 2023 between Laurie Swami, President and CEO of the Nuclear Waste Management Organization and Terence Hubbard, President of the Impact Assessment Agency of Canada and (presumably) a CNSC representative “to continue discussions regarding ongoing efforts towards regulatory efficiency and staff’s readiness for the NWMO’s Deep Geologic Repository (DGR) project” With respect to the meetings held on November 22 2023 and November 29 2023 described above, included in this request are preparatory notes, meeting materials including presentation slides, briefing notes and other meeting documents, and materials related to this meeting produced as follow-up to this meeting, including meeting summaries, meeting notes or meeting reports. With respect to the letter dated November 23, 2023 from President Swami to the Acting CEO of the CNSC and president of IAAC “regarding the activities that are needed to prepare for the regulatory process for NWMO’s DGR [Annex 1]”and Table 1 and Table 2 found in Annex 1 of the letter dated November 23 2023, included in this request are: 1) communications within the Canadian Nuclear Safety, between the Impact Assessment Agency and the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and between the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission and the Nuclear Waste Management Organization in response or followup to the letter of November 23 2023 and attached tables found in Annex 1 of the letter 2) reports of meetings or workshops held within the CNSC or between the CNSC and the Agency or between the CNSC, the NWMO and the Agency related to and/or in followup to the letter of November 23, 2023 from the NWMO 3) briefing notes prepared regarding the preparation or provision of a response to the NWMO to their letter of November 23 2023 and the attached tables 4) any and all response provided to the NWMO to their letter of November 23 2023 including in response to the items identified in Table 1 and Table 2 found in Annex 1 of the letter

The Registry may select the 25 cases at random, provided they meet the above criteria. Clarifications & format •I do not need transcripts—only the digital audio files (MP3 or WAV) and PDFs of the written reasons. •I understand the IRB must comply with s. 19; beyond that, please provide the material unredacted. •If fewer than 25 qualifying written decisions exist for 2024-2025, please provide all that exist and advise

Given recent troubling events in Kelowna involving the Sikh community, including physical and institutional attacks, it is crucial to understand the effectiveness and scope of actions taken by these funded organizations. We have had complaints that local organizations are not doing enough to help the Sikh community, which has faced multiple hate crimes. For instance, the tragic death of Harmandeep Kaur, the attack on Gagandeep Singh, and the systemic issues faced by Dr. Hoonjan are indicative of a broader problem that requires immediate attention. Therefore, I am requesting: Detailed Reports and Evaluations: Information on the specific activities undertaken by these NGOs to combat discrimination against the Sikh community in Kelowna. This should include strategies, program implementations, and outcomes related to tracking and responding to hate crimes. Funding Details: Documents detailing the amounts and conditions of funding provided to these NGOs by IRCC, including any specific requirements related to addressing hate crimes against Sikhs. Redaction of Sensitive Information: While I understand the sensitivity of the information, I request that all personal details such as names, addresses, or other identifiers be redacted to protect individual privacy. The focus of this request is on organizational actions and government oversight, not on individuals per se. Compliance and Accountability Reports: Any available compliance reports or assessments that evaluate the efficacy of funded programs in achieving their anti-discrimination goals.

documentcloud_description: Applications to Canada, under all streams, have questions to determine admissibility. Such as "have you ever been refused a visa or permit, denied entry or order to leave Canada or any other country or territory" amongst other similar questions. There is LOTS of litigation around files that were refused, with many applicants being cited for misrepresentation, even though the typical argument would have been "I didn't understand the question" or "I didn't realize this included all countries in the world". There have been many requests to make these questions simpler and less convoluted. For some reason IRCC has never felt the need to make these questions clearer. One suspects it just acts as an easy way to refuse a file. It's very likely that IRCC has sought numerous legal opinions over the years, whether these opinions are sough internally or externally. I want to see all instances of such opinions, including any and all correspondence related to this issue, including any discussions or meetings or reports or papers or presentations. Ensure to include any and all third party requests related to this, and any response/s given. From 2020-01-01 to 2025-07-09. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. Mark all Cabinet Confidences as non-relevant.

All records created between July 1, 2025 (the approximate discovery date) and October 31, 2025, related to the interstellar object known as "3I/ATLAS" (also designated C/2025 N1). 
To assist in your search, this request includes, but is not limited to, the following types of records: 
1. High-Level Briefings and Assessments: All Briefing Notes, Memoranda to the Minister (MNs), or Advice to the Minister regarding 3I/ATLAS. All Briefing Notes or Memoranda to the Deputy Minister (DM) regarding 3I/ATLAS. All presentation decks (e.g., PowerPoint files) created for senior management (Director General level and above) describing the object's nature, characteristics, observed anomalies (e.g., non-gravitational acceleration, unusual composition), or trajectory. 
2. Internal and External Communications: All internal emails, memos, meeting agendas, and minutes where the "nature," "origin," "composition," "anomalies," "technosignatures," or "non-natural origin" of 3I/ATLAS are discussed. All communications and briefings received by the department from any other government department (OGD) (e.g., DND, NRC, PCO, ISED) or external partner (e.g., NASA, ESA, NORAD, Five Eyes (FVEY) partners, the 'Sky Canada Project' team, or university-affiliated astronomers) regarding 3I/ATLAS. 
3. Scientific and Security Assessments: All scientific or technical analyses, reports, or data summaries created or received by the department regarding 3I/ATLAS's properties (e.g., spectral analysis, composition, radio signals, light curve). Any risk assessment, object characterization report, trajectory analysis, or situational report concerning 3I/ATLAS. All records related to the tasking of Canadian assets (e.g., telescopes, observation time, sensors) to study 3I/ATLAS. 
Clarification: This request is specifically for the interstellar object (comet) 3I/ATLAS. Please provide records in their original electronic format, if possible.

documentcloud_title: 2026-06 - A-2025-16747 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
documentcloud_description: Work Permit Application Processing Time Statistics (2018-2025) Institution: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) Request: Pursuant to the Access to Information Act, I am requesting internal statistical data regarding Work Permit applications processed by IRCC. Scope of Request: Timeframe: January 1, 2018, to March 31, 2025 Format Requested: Excel file (.xlsx or .xls). Please do not provide data as a scanned PDF or print-to-PDF version. Requested Variables: Please provide internal statistical breakdowns of processing times for Work Permit applications in relation to the following factors, presented individually (i.e., separate breakdowns by variable): 1. Previous refusal (Yes / No) 2. Representative type (Lawyer / Consultant / Self-represented) 3. Application Type (International Mobility Program / Temporary Foreign Worker Program) 4. Country of citizenship 5. Country of residence 6. Visa office 7. Final decision outcome (Approved / Refused) 8. Location of application (In-Canada Extension / Outside Canada Initial Work Permit / Inside Canada Initial Work Permit) We understand that IRCC may not have an integrated dataset containing all of these factors cross-referenced in a single table. Separate statistical summaries for each factor are sufficient. Preferred Output: Each breakdown should include: Number of applications. Median and average processing times (calendar days). Standard of deviation if available. For any variable where final decision outcomes are recorded, please include the number of applications approved and refused within each category.

documentcloud_title: 2026-06 - A-2025-24914 - Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada
documentcloud_description: We respectfully request general statistical data related to SUV applications supported by two designated organizations -Spark and Pycap. We are not seeking any private, identifying, or applicant-specific information. Instead, we are requesting aggregate data that will enable us to understand broader trends in SUV processing and ensure any legal submissions made to IRCC are grounded in accurate, current, and verifiable information. While we have requested parallel data through IRCC's ATIP and corporate records channels, a direct response from Spark and Pycap would allow us to proceed more efficiently and with greater precision. We kindly request that you provide a general statistical overview covering the period from January 1, 2017, to May 26, 2025 (or the date of response, whichever is later), based on the following two categories: 1. Applicant-Level Data 2. Commitment Certificate-Level Data (Startup-Level)many were paper vs. online submissions, and how many applicants were Iranian nationals. Commitment Certificate-Level Data: State how many commitment certificates Spark and Pycap have each issued. For each certificate (startup), provide the number of associated applicants and a breakdown of the same data points above. Present both datasets in separate tables. Please provide this data for the period from 2017-01-01 to 2025-05-26 or the date of finalization of this request, whichever is later. Mark all Cabinet Confidences as non-relevant. Remove any records or parts of records that require consultation with other government departments.

3. Date received: The date each FOI was received.
4. Date completed: The date each FOI was completed.
5. Disposition: The disposition for each FOI (records granted in full, in part, denied, etc.).
6. (Not mandatory) Department, division, body or entity: If your tracking system provides details on which part of your organization is being targeted with a request, we would like this information.

We are seeking the above information for FOIs that were completed between July 1, 2024, and March 31, 2026. 

We are only seeking access to data from general records requests, not personal records requests. We are not seeking access to information about FOIs that are not yet completed, or FOIs that were withdrawn, abandoned or transferred to another institution. documentcloud_description: I am seeking documents, guidance, emails, meeting minutes, and related to any information around medical exams related to transition-related care. For example, this would include guidance around how a doctor should evaluate a migrant seeking any kind of permanent status in Canada who has had a bilateral mastectomy ('top surgery'), and if that is something that would make someone ineligible. Or, if there have been explicit directives, meetings, documents, and the like around guiding clinical practitioners to not find someone ineligible because they have undergone clinical, transition-related care. I am unsure who holds this information, but this has come up in discussions with doctors providing clinical exams to transgender migrants as something that has been of discussion within the IRCC. Seeking Briefing notes (including annexes), Discussions/Opinions/Position Papers, Emails (including attachments), Ministerial announcements or news items, Manuals, Policies and directives, Reports, Presentation materials, and Standard Operating Procedures. From 2000-01-01 to 2025-03-05.

I am writing to request a search for records identified as OIC Annual Report: 1999- 2000.
Apparently, the Annual Report reads:
“Go directly to Jail I
In March of 1998 , the House of Commons identified the boundary line when it unanimously passed Collen Beaunier’s private member’s bill which added 67.1 to the Access to Information Act. This is the offence which is therein set out out:
67.1  (1)  No person shall, with intent to deny access under this Act,
a. destroy, mutilate or alter a record.
b. falsify a record or make a false record.
c. conceal a record; or  
d. direct, propose, counsel or cause any person in any manner to do anything mentioned in any of the paragraphs (a) to (c ).
Further the Report reads:
“One was the subject of investigation this year and a case summary may be found at page 44. Two investigations are in progress concerning the possible hiding of destruction of records which were subject of access requests. Their outcome will be reported next year”.

Therefore, under the Information Act I would request a search to discover:
1- A copy of the 1999 Annual OIC Report.
2- A copy of “page 44” that identifies a case summary.
3- A copy of the 2000 OIC Annual Report.
4- Records of OIC conducting OIC investigations of 67.1 violations referred to in the 1999 and 2000 Annual reports.

documentcloud_title: 2026-07 - CLC-A-2024-004 - Canada Lands Company CLC Limited
documentcloud_description: This access to information request aims to obtain copies of all documents and information held by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on lots 3 086 741and 3 086 851 of the Quebec cadastre (hereinafter the "Lots") owned by it in the Saint Hubert borough of the City of Longueil. Specifically, we are making this access to information and documents request to obtain copies of all documents and information held by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on the lots, as well as all relevant information related to the sanitary and/or storm sewer service serving the lots and buildings in the southwest sector of the Saint-Hubert airport, including the buildings located at 4801, rue Leckie and 4801-3, rue Leckie. Without limitation, we wish to obtain all documents related to the pumping station for sanitary and storm sewers located on the Lots and held by Canada Lands Company, for example: Any authorization issued to Canada Lands Company (permits, ministerial authorization, etc.) regarding the construction, installation, and connection of the pumping station located on the Lots (including all documents that are an integral part of and listed in these authorizations); Any request for authorization or permit related to the connection of the pumping station located on the Lots submitted to MELCCFP by Canada Lands Company; Any authorization or permit related to the connection of the pumping station located on the Lots held by Canada Lands Company; Any request for authorization or permit related to the connection to the sanitary and/or storm sewer submitted to MELCCFP for the Lots by Canada Lands Company; Any authorization or permit related to the connection to the sanitary and/or storm sewer issued for the Lots to Canada Lands Company; Any inspection report produced by Canada Lands Company regarding the pumping station located on the Lots; Any notice of non-compliance or any other document regarding the pumping station located on the Lots; Any document regarding the sanitary and/or storm sewer services serving the Lots and buildings located at 4801, rue Leckie and 1111-3, rue Leckie; Any information related to the number and identification of properties served by the pumping station located on the Lots; Any other document held by Canada Lands Company regarding the ownership of the pumping station located on the Lots. Finally, please note that if this includes colour documents (plans, photos), we would like to have colour copies. All documents can be sent to us by email. For any additional information, please do not hesitate to contact the undersigned. We thank you for your attention to this request.

The total budget that has been allocated for ESDC’s Benefits Delivery Modernization program since January 2023 to October 2024, and an inventory of publicly visible releases since that time.   
A yearly total amount is one for "Total budget". (eg, 2022-2023: 301.4 million, etc.) A release could mean a new product or service, a new feature in an existing product or service, a significant improvement to an existing feature (eg, waiting time for X reduced by 90%), or public information about new services.   
An announcement of a future program/service/feature would not qualify as a release by this definition. Information on a release would likely be included in include any final reports and documents that accompany public deliverables (service improvements) from January 1st, 2023, to October 2024. 
In terms of the release (public service improvements) side of things, any new products/features/launches from the BDM program transmittal slips or status updates on the BDM program that include summaries of new services being launched or improvements to existing systems, that might of been captured in briefing notes to senior leaders that accompany SA&As or status updates created by BDM staff for presentations to senior leadership and BDM/TBS governance committees. The minister's LinkedIn announcement on "service delivery initiatives and improvements" which mentions "transforming benefits delivery technology" but does not specify exactly what has been released in this regard.

documentcloud_description: All records, including but not limited to internal memoranda, policy guidance, operational bulletins, briefing notes (including annexes), training materials, program delivery instruction supplements, system design or business rules documentation, standard operating procedures, manuals, and internal correspondence (including emails and attachments), that relate to the assessment and awarding of Additional Points for Canadian Education (15 or 30 points under Express Entry additional factors) in the Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) where a program of study, rather than the institution as a whole, is not eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) at the time of electronic Application for Permanent Residence (e-APR), regardless of the institution's status as a designated learning institution (DLI) or the fact that the institution offers other PGWP-eligible programs, since PGWP eligibility also depends on the field of study. For clarity, this request concerns additional factors points for Canadian education only and does not seek records related solely to core human capital education points. This request includes records that address any of the following: 1. Instructions, guidance, or training provided to officers on how to assess, retain, or remove additional CRS points for Canadian education when the Express Entry system awards such points at the profile stage, but the program of study is determined to be not eligible for a Post-Graduation Work Permit (PGWP) at the time of electronic Application for Permanent Residence (e-APR), including any records that interpret or operationalize the guidance that institutions or programs not eligible for a PGWP at the time of e-APR should not be awarded CRS points for additional factors. 2. Internal clarification or interpretation of Program Delivery Instructions stating that programs of study not eligible for a PGWP at the time of e-APR should not be awarded additional CRS points for Canadian education, and how this requirement is applied during application assessment. 3. Documentation describing the business rules, known limitations, or identified gaps of the Express Entry profile builder in distinguishing between: a. PGWP eligibility of a program of study during the period of study, and b. PGWP eligibility of a program of study at the time of e-APR submission, for the purpose of awarding additional CRS points for Canadian education. 4. Internal communications between policy, program delivery, and systems or digital teams that discuss alignment or discrepancies between Express Entry system logic and officer-facing guidance relating specifically to program-level PGWP eligibility, including field-of-study requirements, and the awarding of additional CRS points for Canadian education. Time frame for this request is: June 1, 2024, to the February 12, 2026. Exclusions: This request does not seek case-specific records, individual applicant files, or personal information. Remove duplicate copies of documents and emails. Remove any records or parts of records that are not related to the subject of the request.

documentcloud_description: Records, statistics, communications and files regarding the North Portal Solar Wall. Specifically, documents relating to the cost of the solar wall, records differentiating the cost of materials and labour to construct and maintain the solar array, including but not limited to planning, implementation, ongoing maintenance. Additionally, documents indicating anticipated efficiency of the solar wall, and actual efficiency since it was installed, documents discussing and implementing the power generation and storage capacity of the solar wall and information on where decisions were made as it relates to building, funding, constructing, storage and maintenance of the solar wall. Also, clear financial breakdowns of how much power the solar wall generates and saves Canada Border Services Agency, what the storage capacity is, and any estimates prior to implementation that were created to support or oppose the building, operation, and ongoing maintenance of the solar wall. Finally, all facts, figures, and statistics that exist as it relates to the solar wall at North Portal, and the historical power usage at North Portal Point of Entry including uptime and downtime of the solar wall, connected power and uptime and downtime of generators on site.

documentcloud_description:
Could you please provide the following details regarding the Canada Greener Homes 0% loan for 10 years? All data should be as on July 23, 2025. 

1. Total Budget: • The total amount of funds allocated to the Canada Greener Homes Loan Program from its launch to date. • Include details on initial budget allocations and any additional funding approvals over time. 

2. Total Funds Disbursed: • The total amount of money disbursed to date from the program budget, broken down by retrofit category (e.g., insulation, windows/doors, heat pumps, solar PV, air-sealing, resiliency measures, etc.), and province and territory, from the program’s launch to date. 

3. Number of Applications (Monthly): • Monthly number of applications received, and number of applications approved, broken down by retrofit category (e.g., insulation, windows/doors, heat pumps, solar PV, air-sealing, resiliency measures, etc.), and province and territory, from the program’s launch to date. 

4. Loan Amount (Monthly): 
• Monthly loan amount requested, and amount approved, broken down by retrofit category (e.g., insulation, windows/doors, heat pumps, solar PV, air-sealing, resiliency measures, etc.), and province and territory, from the program’s launch to date. 

5. Remaining Funds: 
• The current remaining balance of unallocated or unspent funds under the CGH Loan Program. 

6. Budget Forecast: 
• Based on current disbursement trends, an estimate of when the program budget is expected to be fully utilized. 

7. Future Budget Plans: 
• Any documents or communication showing plans to increase the total budget of the CGH Loan Program, including: 
• Approved additional funding (if any). 
• Tentative or proposed funding amounts.
Expected approval or implementation dates. 

8. Documents and Reports: Please provide internal reports, spreadsheets, or official documentation used for: • Budget planning and forecasting. • Monthly/quarterly performance tracking. • Province-wise breakdowns and summaries. Note: 

• Please provide the data in machine-readable format (Excel or CSV preferred). • This request refers specifically to the Canada Greener Homes Loan program (0% interest loan with a 10-year repayment term), not the grant portion.
